key_insight: AGE-MIL improves patient-level prediction by using a patient-level anchor to guide evidence gathering across multiple whole-slide images, instead of treating each slide in isolation.
clinical_relevance: This could make computational pathology outputs more stable and more aligned with how pathologists integrate findings across slides for diagnosis and prognosis.
method: Builds a patient-level anchor from slide representations to capture global pathological context.
Retrieves and integrates diagnostically relevant local patches using the anchor as guidance.
Models risk as an evidence accumulation process to improve weakly supervised learning stability.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on six patient-level prediction tasks across two independent cohorts and outperformed eight state-of-the-art MIL methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on quality of slide representations and multi-WSI coverage, so real-world deployment may vary across centers and staining protocols.
paper_title: AGE-MIL: Anchor-Guided Evidence Learning for Patient-Level Prediction
